# Executive Summary of the Paper

### **Title of the Paper**
Haemodynamic-guided Fluid Administration for the Prevention of Contrast-Induced Acute Kidney Injury: The POSEIDON Randomized Controlled Trial

### **DOI of the Article**
10.1016/S0140-6736(14)60689-9

### **Authors and Journal**
Somjot S Brar et al.; The Lancet; 2014

### **Pubmed Link**
[Link to Study](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(14)60689-9)

### **Pubmed Link**
[Link to Study](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(14)60689-9)

### **Abstract of the Study**
**Rationale & Objective:** The administration of intravenous fluid remains the cornerstone treatment for the prevention of contrast-induced acute kidney injury (CI-AKI). However, no well-defined protocols exist to guide fluid administration in this treatment. This study aimed to establish the efficacy of a new fluid protocol to prevent CI-AKI.

**Study Design:** Randomized, parallel-group, comparator-controlled, single-blind phase 3 trial.

**Setting & Participants:** 396 patients aged 18 years or older undergoing cardiac catheterization with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 60 mL/min per 1.73 m² or less and one or more risk factors.

**Intervention:** Patients were randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to left ventricular end-diastolic pressure-guided volume expansion (n=196) or control group (n=200) who received a standard fluid administration protocol.

**Outcomes:** The primary outcome was the occurrence of CI-AKI, defined as a >25% or >0.5 mg/dL increase in serum creatinine concentration.

**Results:** CI-AKI occurred less frequently in the LVEDP-guided group (6.7% [12/178]) than in the control group (16.3% [28/172]; RR 0.41, 95% CI 0.22-0.79; p=0.005). Adverse events specific to fluid administration were similar between groups.

**Interpretation:** LVEDP-guided fluid administration appears to be safe and effective in preventing CI-AKI in patients undergoing cardiac catheterization.

---

### **1. Bottom Line**
LVEDP-guided fluid administration significantly reduces the incidence of CI-AKI in patients undergoing cardiac catheterization.

---

### **2. Brief Introduction of the Study**
- CI-AKI is associated with increased morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs.
- The study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of a new fluid protocol based on LVEDP in preventing CI-AKI.

---

---

### **3. Design of the Study**
- **Type:** Randomized, parallel-group, comparator-controlled, single-blind phase 3 trial.
- **Population:** 396 patients aged 18 years or older with eGFR ≤ 60 mL/min per 1.73 m² and additional risk factors.
- **Randomization:** 1:1 to LVEDP-guided volume expansion or standard fluid protocol.
- **Endpoints:**
  - **Primary:** Occurrence of CI-AKI.
  - **Secondary:** Components of primary endpoint, major adverse events (all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, renal replacement therapy).

![CONSORT Diagram](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/obsidian-ginnie/assets/main/CONSORT_diagram.png)

---

### **4. Baseline Characteristics of Study Population**
- 396 patients randomized (196 LVEDP, 200 control).
- **Age:** Mean age: 71 (LVEDP), 72 (control).
- **Gender:** Female: 36% (LVEDP), 41% (control).
- **Comorbidities:**
  - Diabetes Mellitus: 52% (LVEDP), 51% (control).
  - Congestive Heart Failure: 16% (LVEDP), 25% (control).

![Table 1: Characteristics of Study Participants at Baseline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/obsidian-ginnie/assets/main/Table1.png)

---

### **5. Inclusion and Exclusion Criteria**
- **Inclusion:**
  - Age ≥ 18 years.
  - eGFR ≤ 60 mL/min per 1.73 m².
  - One or more risk factors (diabetes, CHF, hypertension, age > 75 years).
- **Exclusion:**
  - Inability to obtain consent.
  - Emergency catheterization.
  - Recent contrast exposure.
  - Allergy to contrast media.
  - Acute decompensated heart failure.
  - Severe valvular heart disease.

---

### **6. Clinical Presentation of Patients**
- Patients presented for elective cardiac catheterization.
- Risk factors included diabetes mellitus, CHF, hypertension, and advanced age.

---

---

### **7. Detailed Study Findings and Key Interventions**
- **Primary Outcome:** CI-AKI was significantly lower in the LVEDP-guided group (6.7%) compared to control (16.3%).
- **Secondary Outcomes:**
  - Relative risk of CI-AKI was 0.41 (95% CI 0.22-0.79; p=0.005).
  - Major adverse events at 6 months were lower in the LVEDP-guided group.

---

### **8. Primary Outcomes of the Study**
- **Occurrence of CI-AKI:** 6.7% in LVEDP group vs. 16.3% in control group.
  - **Relative Risk:** 0.41 (95% CI 0.22-0.79; p=0.005).
  - **Number Needed to Treat:** 11 patients to prevent one CI-AKI event.

![Figure 2: Hydration Volumes of Normal Saline Administered in Each Group](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/obsidian-ginnie/assets/main/Figure2.png)

---

---

### **9. Secondary Outcomes of the Study**
- **Major Adverse Events at 6 Months:**
  - 3.1% (LVEDP) vs. 9.5% (control).
  - **Relative Risk:** 0.32 (95% CI 0.13-0.79; p=0.008).
  - **All-Cause Mortality:** 0.5% (LVEDP) vs. 4.0% (control); p=0.037.
  - **Myocardial Infarction:** 2.0% (LVEDP) vs. 6.5% (control); p=0.029.

### **9. Secondary Outcomes of the Study**
- **Major Adverse Events at 6 Months:**
  - 3.1% (LVEDP) vs. 9.5% (control).
  - **Relative Risk:** 0.32 (95% CI 0.13-0.79; p=0.008).
  - **All-Cause Mortality:** 0.5% (LVEDP) vs. 4.0% (control); p=0.037.
  - **Myocardial Infarction:** 2.0% (LVEDP) vs. 6.5% (control); p=0.029.

![Figure 3: Rate of Major Adverse Events in Each Group](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/obsidian-ginnie/assets/main/Figure3.png)

---

### **10. Detailed Results and Statistical Summary**
- **Primary Endpoint:** >25% or 0.5 mg/dL increase in serum creatinine.
  - **LVEDP-guided:** 12/178 (6.7%).
  - **Control:** 28/172 (16.3%).
  - **Relative Risk:** 0.41 (95% CI 0.22-0.79; p=0.005).
- **Secondary Endpoints:**
  - **>25% Increase in Serum Creatinine:**
    - **LVEDP-guided:** 6.7%.
    - **Control:** 15.7%.
  - **>0.5 mg/dL Increase in Serum Creatinine:**
    - **LVEDP-guided:** 2.8%.
    - **Control:** 6.4%.

![Table 2: Occurrence of CI-AKI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/obsidian-ginnie/assets/main/Table2.png)

---

### **11. Subgroup Analysis and Adverse Events**
- **Subgroup Analysis:**
  - Significant reduction in CI-AKI across various subgroups (e.g., diabetes, contrast volume).
  - **Diabetes:**
    - **LVEDP-guided:** 12.1%.
    - **Control:** 22.2%.
  - **Sex:**
    - **Male:** LVEDP-guided: 3.4%, Control: 10.9%.
    - **Female:** LVEDP-guided: 12.9%, Control: 23.9%.

![Table 3: Occurrence of CI-AKI in Prespecified Patient Subgroups](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/obsidian-ginnie/assets/main/Table3.png)

- **Adverse Events:**
  - Hydration terminated early in three patients from each group due to shortness of breath.

### **12. Discussion**
- **Major Findings:**
  - LVEDP-guided fluid administration significantly reduces CI-AKI incidence and major adverse events.
  - Effective in patients with stable renal insufficiency undergoing cardiac catheterization.
- **Mechanisms:**
  - Volume expansion may reduce contrast-mediated injury by expanding plasma volume and reducing renin activation.
- **Limitations:**
  - Not suitable for patients with acute decompensated heart failure or severe valvular heart disease.
  - Partially blinded study design.

### **13. Statistical Tests Used in the Study**
- **Wilcoxon Rank Sum Test:** For continuous variables.
- **χ² or Fisher's Exact Test:** For categorical variables.
- **Logistic Regression:** For assessing consistency of treatment effect across subgroups.
- **Kaplan-Meier Method and Log-rank Test:** For major adverse events analysis.

### **14. Main Weaknesses of this Paper**
- Partially blinded design.
- Exclusion of certain high-risk populations.
- Limited generalizability due to study population characteristics.

### **15. Issues Authors Failed to Address and Further Research Questions**
- Need for validation in broader populations.
- Assessment of non-invasive measures for intravascular volume status.
-

 Long-term outcomes and cost-effectiveness of LVEDP-guided hydration strategy.
